/-!
# Erdős Problem 13

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/13](https://www.erdosproblems.com/13)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset Nat

namespace Erdos13

/--
A finite set of naturals `A` is said to be forbidden-triple-free if for all `a, b, c ∈ A`,
if `a < min(b, c)` then `a` does not divide `b + c`.
-/
def IsForbiddenTripleFree (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ∀ c ∈ A, a < min b c → ¬ (a ∣ b + c)

/--
If $A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ is a set with no $a, b, c \in A$ such that $a | (b+c)$ and
$a < \min(b,c)$, then $|A| \le N/3 + O(1)$. This has been solved by Bedert [Be23].

[Be23] Bedert, B., _On a problem of Erdős and Sárközy about sequences with no term dividing
the sum of two larger terms_. arXiv:2301.07065 (2023).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos13.lean#L8261"]
theorem erdos_13 : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 N, IsForbiddenTripleFree A →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / 3 + C := by
  sorry

/--
A general version asks, for a fixed $r \in \mathbb{N}$, if a set
$A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ has no $a \in A$ and $b_1, ..., b_r \in A$ such that
$a | (b_1 + ... + b_r)$ and $a < \min(b_1, ..., b_r)$, then is it true that
$|A| \le N/(r+1) + O(1)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_13.variants.general : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ,
    ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 N,
    (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ (b : Fin r → ℕ), (∀ i, b i ∈ A) → (∀ i, a < b i) →
      ¬ (a ∣ ∑ i, b i)) →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / (r + 1) + C := by
  sorry

end Erdos13

reformulations.difference: Lean includes r = 0 and N = 0, extending the usual positive-parameter formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For r = 0 the unique empty tuple has sum 0, and every a divides 0. Thus the forbidden-sum hypothesis holds exactly when A is empty, and this additional case satisfies the bound with C = 0. For N = 0, A ⊆ Icc 1 0 also forces A to be empty; replacing any positive-N witness C by max C 0 handles this case. The full right-hand side is therefore equivalent to its restriction to positive r and N. This equivalence was proved as Review.general_positive_parameters_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes:
All three declarations were checked; no mathematical defect was found. The main predicate correctly permits repeated larger summands, as Bedert's definition and arguments do. The general theorem states the exactly-r-summands variant, with C allowed to depend on r but not on N or A. Lean checks verified its r = 2 specialization, denominator positivity, and boundary cases; small finite examples were also evaluated.

The live Erdős Problems page was blocked by Cloudflare. The accessible 2026-08-30 snapshot explicitly gives N/(r+1)+O(1), matching Lean, and records the main problem as PROVED (LEAN). An older snapshot instead printed r−1; that obsolete wording is not evidence of a defect in this file. No status discrepancy was found in the accessible sources.

The exact linked formal proof and all three non-Mathlib dependencies compiled unchanged in /workspace/review/external. Its #print axioms output was [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], confirming the formal_proof record without sorryAx or custom axioms.
